questions.q: The vehicles carrying inflammable fluids usually have metallic chains touching the ground :
options: To protect tyres from catching dirt from ground
To conduct excess charge due to air friction to ground and prevent sparking
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Static charge is developed due to air friction. This can result in combustion. So, metallic chains is used to discharge excess charge.

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a point charge $Q$~is placed at the centre of conducting spherical shell of inner radius $a$ and outer radius $b$. The electric field due to charge $Q$ in three different regions $I, II\text{and}III$ is given by : $( I: r b )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In region I, due to charge at centre, electric field will be present.

But in region II, electric field will be zero as electric field inside material of conductor is zero.

Again for outside region, net charges enclosed is not zero and therefore electric field will exist.

questions.q: An electric dipole of moment $\overset{→}{p} = \left(- \overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \times {10}^{- 29}\text{C m}$ at the origin  \left(0,0, 0\right)$ . The electric field due to this dipole at $\overset{→}{\text{r}} = + \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$ (note that $\overset{→}{r} ∙ \overset{→}{p} = 0$ ) is parallel to:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As& $\overset{→}{r} \cdot \overset{→}{p} = 0$, this means that~$\overset{→}{r}$~is perpendicular to~$\overset{→}{p}$.

For an electric dipole, electric field at equatorial position is antiparallel to~$\overset{→}{p}$.

$⇒ \overset{→}{E} = - \lambda\overset{→}{p}$,

where,~$\lambda$~is an arbitrary positive constant.

$⇒ \overset{→}{E} = - \lambda\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \times {10}^{- 29}Cm^{- 2}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{E} = \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \times {10}^{- 29}Cm^{- 2}$

For~$\lambda = \dfrac{1}{10- 29}$~

$⇒ \overset{→}{E} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right)Cm^{- 2}$

$⇒ \sigma =0 . 424 \times {10}^{- 9}Cm^{- 2}

$

questions.q: Two point charges $Q$~each are placed at a distance $d$ apart. A third point charge $q$ is placed at a distance $x$ from mid-point on the perpendicular bisector. The value of $x$~at which charge $q$ will experience the maximum Coulomb's force is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The distance between& $q$~and~$Q$~is~$r = \sqrt{x^{2} + \left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)2} = \sqrt{x^{2} + \dfrac{d2}{4}}$.

The force between~$q$~and~$Q$~will be~$F = \dfrac{kqQ}{r2}$.

From the given figure we can see that only vertical components of the forces will add, and the~horizontal components will get cancelled out.~Therefore,

${F}_{net} = \dfrac{2kqQ}{r2}cos\theta = \dfrac{2kqQ}{r2} \times \dfrac{x}{r} = \dfrac{kqQx}{\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{d2}{4}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}$

For force to be maximum,~$\dfrac{d {F}_{net}}{d x} = 0 .$

$⇒ kqQ\left[\dfrac{\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{d2}{4}\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - x \times \dfrac{3}{2}\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{d2}{4}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} \times 2x}{\left(\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{d2}{4}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}\right)2}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \left(x^{2} + \dfrac{d2}{4}\right) = 3x^{2} ⇒ 2x^{2} = \dfrac{d2}{4} ⇒ x = \dfrac{d}{2\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length $L$ is placed between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor having electric field $E$ , as shown in figure. Its bob has mass $m$ and charge $q$ . The time period of the pendulum is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Two forces will be acting on the mass& $m$, gravity force and force by the electric field.

Thus, the effective force $= \sqrt{{\left(qE\right)}^{2} + {\left(mg\right)}^{2}}$
From force equation,~${g}_{eff} = \sqrt{g^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{qE}{m}\right)}^{2}}$
Time period of the pendulum is~\left(T\right) = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{{g}_{eff}}}$
$= 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{\sqrt{g^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{qE}{m}\right)}^{2}}}}$

$

questions.q: The electric field in a region is given by $\overset{→}{E} = \left(Ax + B\right)\overset{^}{i},$ where $E$ is in $NC^{- 1}$ and $x$ is in metres. The values of constants are $A = 20SI$ unit and $B = 10SI$ unit. If the potential at $x = 1$ is ${V}_{1}$ and that at $x = - 5$ is ${V}_{2},$ then ${V}_{1} - {V}_{2}$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${V}_{1} - {V}_{2} = - ∫ E . dx$
$= - \mathop{∫}_{- 5}^{1}\left(ax + b\right)dx$
$= {- \left[\dfrac{ax^{2}}{2} + bx\right]}_{- 5}^{1}$
$= - \left[ $\$left(\dfrac{a}{2} +b\right) - \left(\dfrac{\text{a} \times 25}{2} -$5b\right)\right]$
$= - $\$left[\dfrac{20}{2} +$10 - 250 + 50\right]$
$= 180V$

A point charge causes an electric flux of $-2 \times 10^4 \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrmC^{-1}$ to pass through a spherical Gaussian surface of 8.0 cm radius, centred on the charge. The value of the point charge is :

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Flux }(\phi)=\frac{\theta_{\text {inc }}}{\epsilon_0} \\ & \begin{aligned} \theta_{\text {inc }} & =\epsilon_0 \phi \\ \quad= & -17.7 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two charges of each magnitude $0 . 01C$ and~separated by a distance of $0 . 4mm$ constitute an~electric dipole. If the dipole is placed in an uniform~electric field $\overset{→}{E}$ of $10dyne \cdot C^{- 1}$ making ${30}^{∘}$ angle with~$\overset{→}{E},$& the magnitude of torque acting on dipole is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the dipole moment is given by

\left|\overset{⇀}{p}\right| = q \left|\overset{⇀}{d}\right| . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the dipole moment.

$\$begin{cases}\left|\overset{⇀}{p}\right|$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 0 . 01C \times0 . 4mm $\times $\dfrac{1m}{{10}^{3}mm}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 4 . 0 $\times {10}^{- 6}$C \cdotm\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the torque on the dipole in the electric field is given by

$| \overset{→}{τ} | = | \overset{→}{p} $\times \overset{→}{E} | . . . \left($2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to calculate the required torque.

$\$begin{cases}\left|\overset{⇀}{τ}\right|$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 4 . 0 $\times {10}^{- 6}$C $\cdot$m $\times$10dyne $\cdot$C^{- 1} $\times $\dfrac{1N}{{10}^{5}dyne} \timessin30 ° \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 2 $\times {10}^{- 10}$Nm\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Two charges $q$ and $3q$ are separated by a distance ‘$r$’ in air. At a distance $x$ from charge $q$, the resultant electric field is zero. The value of $x$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: \left(\overset{→}{E}net\right)P = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{kq}{x2} = \dfrac{k \times 3q}{\left(r - x\right)2}$

$⇒ \left(r - x\right)2 = 3x^{2}$

$⇒ r - x = \sqrt{3}x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{r}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$

$

questions.q: Concentric metallic hollow spheres of radii R and 4R hold charges ${Q}_{1}$~and~${Q}_{2}$~respectively. Given that~surface charge densities of the concentric spheres are equal, the potential difference~$V\left(R\right) - V ( 4R )$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As given the surface charge density for both the spheres is same, hence

${σ}_{1} = {σ}_{2} ∴ \dfrac{Q1}{A1} = \dfrac{Q2}{A2} ⇒ \dfrac{Q1}{4\piR^{2}} = \dfrac{Q2}{4\pi\left(4R\right)2} ∴ {Q}_{2} = 16{Q}_{1}$

From above diagram, the electric potential~for both the spheres is~

${V}_{Inner} = \dfrac{KQ1}{R} + \dfrac{KQ2}{4R} = \dfrac{K}{R}\left({Q}_{1} + \dfrac{16{Q}_{1}}{4}\right) = \dfrac{5{KQ}_{1}}{R} .$

In the same way for outer sphere,~

${V}_{Outer} = \dfrac{KQ1}{4R} + \dfrac{KQ2}{4R} = \dfrac{K}{4R}\left(16{Q}_{1} + {Q}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{17{KQ}_{1}}{4R}$.

Now the potential difference is,

$∆ V = {V}_{inner} - {V}_{outer}$

$= \dfrac{5{KQ}_{1}}{R} - \dfrac{17{KQ}_{1}}{4R} = \dfrac{3{Q}_{1}}{16{πε}_{0}R}$.

questions.q: An electric dipole of mass m, charge q, and length \(l\) is placed in a uniform electric field \$(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=\mathrm{E}}_{0} \hat{i}\). When the dipole is rotated slightly from its equilibrium position and released, the time period of its oscillations will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\tau=P E_0 \sin \theta$ If $\theta$ is small $\begin{aligned} \tau & =-\left(P E_0\right) \theta \\ I & =m\left(\frac{l}{2}\right)^2 \cdot 2=\frac{m l^2}{2} \\ T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m l^2}{2 \cdot P E_0}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m l^2}{2 \cdot q / E_0}} \\ T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m l}{2 q E_0}} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let a total charge $2Q$ be distributed in a sphere of radius $R,$ with the charge density given by $ρ ( r ) = kr,$ where $r$ is the distance from the centre. Two charges $A$ and $B$ , of $- Q$ each, are placed on diametrically opposite points, at equal distance, a, from the centre. If $A$ and $B$ do not experience any force, then:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As total charge on sphere is $= 2Q$
$2Q = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}\left(kr\right)\left(4\pir^{2}dr\right) ⇒ k{πr}^{4} = 2Q$
Charged enclosed in the sphere of radius $a$~
$q = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{a}kr \times 4\pir^{2}dr = k\pia^{4}$
As force on $Q$ is zero
$\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{Q^{2}}{{\left(2a\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{k\pia^{4}}{4\pi{ε}_{0} \times a^{2}} \times Q$
$⇒ \dfrac{Q^{2}}{4} = k\pia^{4}Q$
$= a^{4}\left(\dfrac{2Q}{R^{4}}\right)Q$
$R^{4} = 8a^{4} ⇒ R = {8}^{\dfrac{1}{4}}a$ or $a = {8}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}}R$

questions.q:
Three identical charged balls each of charge $2C$ are suspended from a common point $P$ by silk threads of $2m$ each (as shown in figure). They form an equilateral triangle of side $1m$.

The ratio of net force on a charged ball to the force between any two charged balls will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We have force between any two charge${F}_{1} = {F}_{2} = \dfrac{q2}{4\pi{ε}_{0}l^{2}} = F$

Resultant electrostatics force~${F}_{R} = \sqrt{{F}_{1}^{2} + {F}_{2}^{2} + 2{F}_{1}{F}_{2}cos60 °}$

$= \sqrt{F^{2} + F^{2} + \left(2F^{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{3F^{2}}$

So, the ratio of net force on a charged ball to the force between any charged balls~is~

$⇒ \dfrac{FR}{F} = \sqrt{3}$

questions.q: Which of the following correctly represents the variation of electric potential $( V )$ of a charged spherical conductor of radius $( R )$ with radial distance $( r )$ from the centre?

questions.solution:
As electric field inside the charged conducting sphere is zero, therefore potential will be constant for the inside part.

For outside part, electric potential decreases as& $V = \dfrac{kq}{r}$& and the conducting sphere behaves like a point charge concentrated at the centre.&

questions.q:
The volume charge density of a sphere of radius $6m$ is $2\mu C{cm}^{- 3}$. The number of lines of force per unit surface area coming out from the surface of the sphere is _____~$\times {10}^{10}NC^{- 1} .$

[Given : Permittivity of vacuum~${ϵ}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}C^{2}N^{- 1} - m^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $ρ = 2\mu C{cm}^{- 3}$~and~$R = 6m$.

Number~of lines of force~per unit area $=$ electric field at surface$= \dfrac{KQ}{R2}$

$E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{ρ\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}}{R2}$~

$E = \dfrac{ρR}{3{ϵ}_{0}} = \dfrac{2 \times 6}{3 \times 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}} = 0 . 45 \times {10}^{12}NC^{- 1}$

$= 45 \times {10}^{10}NC^{- 1}$

questions.q:
A positive ion $A$ and a negative ion $B$ has charges $6.67 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ and $9.6 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{C}$, and masses $19.2 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$ and $9 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$ respectively. At an instant, the ions are separated by a certain distance r. At that instant the ratio of the magnitudes of electrostatic force to gravitational force is $P \times 10^{45}$, where the value of 10$P$ is $\qquad$
(Take $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrmC^{-1}$ and universal gravitational constant as $6.67 \times 10^{-11} \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrm{~kg}^{-2}$ )
Assume that charge may not be an integral multiple of electrons.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
F_e & =\frac{k q_1 q_2}{r^2} \\
F_g & =\frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2} \\
\frac{F_e}{F_g} & =\frac{k q_1 q_2}{G m_1 m_2} \\
& =\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-19} \times 9.6 \times 10^{-10}}{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 19.2 \times 10^{-27} \times 9 \times 10^{-27}} \\
& =\frac{10^{-20}}{2 \times 10^{-65}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electron revolves around an infinite cylindrical wire having uniform linear charge density& $2 \times {10}^{- 8}Cm^{- 1}$ in circular path under the influence of attractive electrostatic field as shown in the figure. The velocity of electron with which it is revolving is ______________~$\times {10}^{6}ms^{- 1}$. Given mass of electron~$= 9 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The electric field is given by&

$E = \left(\dfrac{2k\lambda}{r}\right)

The required centripetal force is~

$F = \left(\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}\right)$

The force due to the field~is equal to the required centripetal force,

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{2k\lambda}{r}\right)e = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k\lambdae}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 9 \times {10}^{9} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}{9 \times {10}^{- 31}}}$

$= \sqrt{1 . 6 \times 4 \times {10}^{13}} = 4 \times 2 \times {10}^{6}ms^{- 1}$

$= 8 \times {10}^{6}ms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: Two charges of $- 4\mu C$ and $+ 4\mu C$ are placed at the points $A ( 1, 0, 4 ) m$ and $B ( 2, - 1, 5 ) m$ located in an electric field $\overset{→}{E} = 0 . 20\overset{^}{i}V{cm}^{- 1}$. The magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole is $8\sqrt{\alpha} \times {10}^{- 5}Nm$, where \alpha =_________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given the electric field is

$\begin{cases}\overset{→}{E} & = & 0 . 20\overset{^}{i}\dfrac{V}{cm} \\ & = & 20\overset{^}{i}\dfrac{V}{m}\end{cases}$

The formula for calculating the torque is

$\overset{→}{τ} = \overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{E} . . . \left(1\right)$

where,

\begin{cases}\overset{→}{p}$& = & q\overset{→}{l} \\ & = & 4 \times \left[\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \left(-1\right)\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(1\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right)\right] \\ & = & 4\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\muCm\end{cases}$

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

$\overset{→}{τ} = ( 4\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} ) \times {10}^{- 6} \times (20\overset{^}{i} ) Nm = ( 8\overset{^}{k} + 8\overset{^}{j} ) \times {10}^{- 5}Nm ⇒ \left|\overset{→}{τ}\right| = $\sqrt{{8}^{2} + {8}^{2}} \times {10}^{- 5}$Nm = $8\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 5}$Nm$

Hence, $\alpha =2.

$
